terra.problem: The clipboard line invents a detail about the scene and implies a clipboard may appear later.
The quiz and pop-quiz jokes use a school scenario and echo the lesson’s questions.
Saying the crowd was just there to be fed assigns a reason for their presence that the text does not give.
The explanation attributes a calculation and a feeling about the result to the disciples without marking them as Papa Dorin’s guesses.
“That’s a different story” invokes another feeding account without a reference.
The numbers were not simply flipped: the selected answer says two loaves and one fish, not two loaves and five fish.
The text says Jesus directed the crowds to sit, not explicitly that everybody sat down.
The passage says Jesus spoke a blessing; it does not say He gave thanks.
The explanation adds an unreferenced fact about Zion and places Jesus on a hillside by a lake, details not given in this passage.
“Wrong direction” says the baker’s answer is wrong, which the voice rules prohibit.
Exodus 19:20 says Moses went up Mount Sinai; it does not establish the stated fact that he received the law there.
The explanation states a purpose for sitting and rules out a nap, neither of which the text says.
“My accountant” invents an accountant for Papa Dorin, adding to his world.
“Not even close” is a negative, potentially shaming response to the baker’s answer.
